text:
joe: Hey team — hitting a breaking error on embeddings batch calls. Started after we switched to dynamic batching. Calls sometimes succeed, sometimes return 400 with 'DimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 1024'. We're always calling the same model id in our client (embed-large-v2).

maria: Sorry you're seeing this, joe. Can you paste a minimal repro request and the exact error payload? Also which SDK/version?

joe: Using our in-house client (wraps the REST /embeddings). Payload like:
```json
{
  "model": "embed-large-v2",
  "input": ["a short sentence", "another sentence"]
}
```
Error body: `{\"error\":\"DimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 1024\", \"batch_id\": \"b-9f2d\"}`
SDK: pinned to our internal wrapper, which uses ruby http calls (no official Redwood SDK).

raj: Quick hypothesis: dynamic batching may be grouping requests for different active model variants (quantized or older model) and the runtime raises when tensors have different dims. Can you confirm both requests are arriving with model field set? If a request lacks model or has an older model alias, it could be routed to a different backend.

joe: We always include model in the body. I logged the outgoing traffic and both show model: embed-large-v2. No mix of models on client side.

ingrid: Pinging infra logs for batch b-9f2d — @deploy-bot can you fetch the runtime batch dump for that batch id?

deploy-bot: Batch dump for b-9f2d:
```
batch_id: b-9f2d
requests: [r-1201, r-1202, r-1203]
routing_keys: [model_key: embed-large-v2, model_key: <null>, model_key: embed-large-v2]
prediction_shapes: [1536, 1024, 1536]
error: DimensionMismatch at merge_kv_cache: expected 1536 got 1024
```

sam: A null model_key in routing_keys is the smoking gun — that request likely was missing the model header at the gateway or the header got dropped in transit. The batching router uses the routing key to group compatible requests. If dynamic batching isn't including model dimension as part of the key, it might still join incompatible requests.

maria: For an immediate mitigation for joe: Can you try setting max_batch_size=1 in your request (if your client passes batching hints) or in your account's default batching policy? That will avoid multi-request merges while we investigate. Also try disabling dynamic batching if that's configurable for your plan.

joe: I can hack client to send sequential single-request calls as a test. Do you have a curl I can run pointing directly to the embeddings endpoint to reproduce?

raj: Try this curl (replace KEY and URL):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
If you run multiple curl processes concurrently you'll reproduce the dynamic batching path. Also run with model intentionally omitted for one of them to see the null routing_key case.

joe: Ran concurrent 10 curls, I see 2 out of 10 failing with the same DimensionMismatch. Attached the request logs showing one of the failing calls had no model header in the raw HTTP capture (weird, our wrapper always includes it).

ingrid: That suggests a gateway bug where under load intermittent requests lose model metadata. We'll search gateway logs around the failing request timestamps. @raj can you confirm whether the batching router also keys on embedding vector length or only model id?

raj: Current router keys are: (model_id, model_variant, customer_tier). It does not explicitly include expected_embedding_dim. So if model_id is null, it allows mixing based on variant null matching. We should update router to include the model's output_dim or to treat null model ids as non-batchable.

sam: Ops note: there's an active deploy yesterday that touched the gateway header parsing code. Rolling that change back in can be a quick rollback path if we confirm correlation with failure times.

maria: For customer-visible mitigations: 1) set max_batch_size=1 or disable dynamic batching on your API key; 2) pin the model to a stable alias (explicit & canonical model name) in every request; 3) temporarily throttle concurrent clients. We'll open an internal incident since this affects correctness.

joe: I tried max_batch_size=1 via header X-Redwood-Max-Batch: 1 and immediate success on the same load. Thanks, this is good as a stopgap.

deploy-bot: Roll status: gateway/parse-headers v2.3.7 deployed 2026-03-02T17:08:14Z by sam — rollout to all nodes completed. No automatic rollback recorded.

ingrid: Correlating failure window with that deploy — looks like failure rate spiked after 17:12Z. We'll revert v2.3.7 to v2.3.6 on gateway nodes now. ETA ~12 minutes.

raj: Long-term fix ideas: - include expected_embedding_dim in routing key - treat missing model_id as non-batchable (force batch isolation) - add stronger schema checks early at gateway to reject requests missing model field with 4xx and avoid mis-batching - add unit tests for header parse under concurrency

sam: Revert started. Rolling back gateways...

deploy-bot: Rollback complete: gateway/parse-headers v2.3.6 active on all nodes.

ingrid: Can anyone rerun the concurrent repro (joe) to confirm if rollback fixed it?

joe: Reran the same concurrent test with header X-Redwood-Max-Batch removed — 0/50 failures now. Looks resolved for my case.

maria: Great — we'll keep this incident open and follow up with a patch to the router. I opened issue IN-7192 to track: root cause gateway header parse bug caused intermittent null model routing_key + batching router not including embedding_dim, which together produced DimensionMismatch.

raj: Assigned to eng-runtime and eng-gateway. Proposed patch: 1) enforce model_id presence in gateway request parsing and return 400 if missing; 2) update batching key to include model_output_dim; 3) add integration test that simulates mixed-dim requests to confirm router rejects combos.

maria: Joe — we'll provide a postmortem and timeline. For now, we'll credit your quick repro. Any preference on follow-up (email/zoom)?

joe: Email summary is fine. Appreciate the quick triage.

sam: After-action items: create canary for header parser deploys, increase header parse test coverage, and add a metric for null-routing-keys per minute so we detect this early.

maria: Closing loop: workaround (max_batch_size=1) and rollback fixed customer impact. We'll update you when fix merges and a safe re-deploy plan is in place. :slightly_smiling_face:
